References

Ehrig, H., Ehrig, K., Prange, U., and Taentzer, G. (2006). Fundamentals of Algebraic Graph Transformation. Springer. [Double-pushout rewriting and the gluing conditions.]

Goguen, J. A., and Burstall, R. M. (1992). Institutions: Abstract model theory for specification and programming. Journal of the ACM, 39(1), 95–146.

Johnson, M., Rosebrugh, R., and Wood, R. J. (2002). Entity-relationship-attribute designs and sketches. Theory and Applications of Categories, 10(3), 94–112. [Schemas as finite-limit sketches; instances as Set-models.]

Crossley, J. N., Poernomo, I. H., and Wirsing, M. (2000). Extraction of structured programs from specification proofs. In D. Bert, C. Choppy, and P. D. Mosses (Eds.), Recent Trends in Algebraic Development Techniques (WADT'99, Château de Bonas, 15–18 September 1999), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 1827 (pp. 419–437). Springer.

Poernomo, I. H., and Crossley, J. N. (2001). Protocols between programs and proofs. In K.-K. Lau (Ed.), Logic Based Program Synthesis and Transformation (LOPSTR 2000), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 2042. Springer, Berlin Heidelberg. DOI 10.1007/3-540-45142-0_2.

Poernomo, I. H., Wirsing, M., and Crossley, J. N. (2005). Adapting Proofs-as-Programs: The Curry–Howard Protocol. Monographs in Computer Science. Springer, New York. Hardcover ISBN 978-0-387-23759-6. DOI 10.1007/0-387-28183-5.

Snodgrass, R. T. (2000). Developing Time-Oriented Database Applications in SQL. Morgan Kaufmann. [Valid time, transaction time; the temporal query taxonomy.]

Vos, R. (2020). Arriving late: bi-temporal backdated adjustments. roelantvos.com, with the accompanying technical paper Data Warehouse Patterns: Bitemporal Backdated Adjustments. [The worked mechanics of splitting validity intervals when corrections arrive late.]

Spivak, D. I. (2012). Functorial data migration. Information and Computation, 217, 31–51.

Spivak, D. I. (2014). Category Theory for the Sciences. MIT Press. [Ologs; schemas as categories.]

ISO/IEC. (2011). SQL:2011 (ISO/IEC 9075:2011), temporal table features.

Danielsson, N. A., Hughes, J., Jansson, P., and Gibbons, J. (2006). Fast and loose reasoning is morally correct. POPL ’06, 206–217. [License for reasoning in the idealized setting and transporting conclusions.]

Akidau, T., et al. (2015). The Dataflow Model: A practical approach to balancing correctness, latency, and cost in massive-scale, unbounded, out-of-order data processing. PVLDB, 8(12), 1792–1803. [Event time, processing time, watermarks, late data.]

Akidau, T., Chernyak, S., and Lax, R. (2018). Streaming Systems. O'Reilly.

Argyris, C. (1977). Double loop learning in organizations. Harvard Business Review, 55(5), 115–124. [Single-loop corrects the action; double-loop revises the governing variables.]

Popper, K. R. (1963). Conjectures and Refutations: The Growth of Scientific Knowledge. Routledge. [Falsifiability; science as institutionalized error-correction.]

von Foerster, H. (1981). Observing Systems. Intersystems Publications. [Second-order cybernetics: the cybernetics of observing systems.]

Beyer, B., Jones, C., Petoff, J., and Murphy, N. R. (Eds.) (2016). Site Reliability Engineering. O'Reilly. [Blameless postmortem culture, ch. 15.]

Huang, J., et al. (2024). Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet. ICLR 2024. [Introspective self-correction degrades performance; falsification must be external.]

Panickssery, A., Bowman, S. R., and Feng, S. (2024). LLM evaluators recognize and favor their own generations. NeurIPS 2024. [Self-preference bias; judge must not be author.]

Sharma, M., et al. (2023). Towards understanding sycophancy in language models. ICLR 2024. [Preference training rewards agreement over accuracy.]

Manheim, D., and Garrabrant, S. (2018). Categorizing variants of Goodhart's law. arXiv:1803.04585. [The adversarial variant: measures captured by what users want them to say.]

Huang, K., Jin, Y., et al. (2025). Automated hypothesis validation with agentic sequential falsifications. ICML 2025. [The POPPER system: LLM agents designing falsification experiments.]

Stojanovic, L. (2004). Methods and Tools for Ontology Evolution. PhD thesis, Universität Karlsruhe (TH). [Usage-driven ontology evolution in the KAON framework; pre-LLM ontology evolution from usage logs — the tradition the reflexive loop extends.]

Kim, Y., et al. (2025). Towards a science of scaling agent systems. Google Research, Google DeepMind and MIT. [Error amplification by topology: 17.2x uncoordinated vs 4.4x orchestrated.]

Pourreza, M., and Rafiei, D. (2023). DIN-SQL: Decomposed in-context learning of text-to-SQL with self-correction. NeurIPS 2023. [The error taxonomy; schema linking as dominant failure class.]

Lei, F., et al. (2024). Spider 2.0: Evaluating language models on real-world enterprise text-to-SQL workflows. ICLR 2025.

Li, J., et al. (2023). Can LLM already serve as a database interface? A big bench for large-scale database grounded text-to-SQLs (BIRD). NeurIPS 2023.

Liu, N. F., et al. (2024). Lost in the middle: How language models use long contexts. TACL, 12. [Positional non-uniformity of attention.]

Hsieh, C.-P., et al. (2024). RULER: What's the real context size of your long-context language models? arXiv:2404.06654. [Claimed vs effective context length.]

Modarressi, A., et al. (2025). NoLiMa: Long-context evaluation beyond literal matching. ICML 2025.

Dell'Acqua, F., et al. (2023). Navigating the jagged technological frontier. Harvard Business School Working Paper 24-013. [Consultant productivity inside and outside the AI capability frontier.]

Anthropic (2026). How AI assistance impacts the formation of coding skills. [Comprehension 50% vs 67%; the shallow-review failure mode.]

Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Article 17; Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4), Article 40; Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR), Article 77. [The two clocks: erasure and mandated retention.]

NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 (2014). Guidelines for Media Sanitization. [Cryptographic erase as a sanitization method.]

ISO/IEC 11179-4. Metadata registries — Part 4: Formulation of data definitions. [The definition quality gate.]

Note: industry figures cited in the text (Gartner data-quality cost estimates, agent-adoption and metadata-maturity percentages, conversational-AI market projections, and vendor benchmark results) are attributed inline to their sources at point of use. Vendor and practitioner sources cited by name and date — Snowflake (Cortex Analyst and AISQL engineering blogs, semantic-view guidance, 2024–2026), Databricks (Genie documentation), Google Cloud (Looker Conversational Analytics documentation and blog, 2025), dbt Labs (semantic-layer benchmark, 2026), AtScale (text-to-SQL benchmark, 2024), Strategy (token cost and accuracy benchmark, 2026), Malloy documentation, Meta (probabilistic flakiness, 2020), Airbnb (Midas and Data Quality Score), the Fivetran star-schema-versus-wide-table benchmark, Reis (2025), Tabb (2023), Verraes (2019), and Vos (bi-temporal backdated adjustments) — are engineering publications subject to revision.
